blocks.text: The imperative may be formed from both the imperfective and the perfective verbs. It is formed from the 3rd person plural of the present tense or the perfective future by dropping the ending (**-ют**, **-ут**, **-ят**, **-ат**) and adding the endings of the imperative:

head: After a vowel
After a single consonant, 1st pers. sing. stressed
After a single consonant, 1st pers. sing. not stressed

points: After two or more consonants the imperative has always the ending **-и**(**те**) regardless of the stress: **смотрите**, **помните**.

Verbs ending in **-ся** follow the same rules, but the ending **-ся** (after **-й** or **-ь**) or **-сь** (after **-и** or **-те**) should be added: **брей** — **брейся** — **брейтесь**; **готовь** — **готовься** — **готовьтесь**; **учи** — **учись** — **учитесь**.

Imperfective verbs of the type of **давать**, **вставать**, which drop the suffix «**ва**» in the present tense, restore it in the imperative: **давайте**, **вставайте**. The imperative from **есть** is **ешьте**; from **пить** — **пейте**; from **бить** — **бейте**; from **быть** — **будьте**; from **лечь** — **лягте** (mostly replaced by **ложись** — **ложитесь**).

items: Будьте добры купить для меня 5 марок.
Be so kind as to buy me 5 stamps.

blocks.text: The English expressions "let (have) him (her, them) do it" are rendered in Russian by «**пусть (пускай)**» with the present imperfective or the future perfective:

Constructions of the type "Let's do it" are rendered by **давайте** + infinitive of the imperfective, or **давайте** + perfective future. In affirmative imperfective constructions «**будем**» is usually omitted: *Давайте (будем) разговаривать!* In the perfective aspect the word «**давайте**» may be omitted, the particle **-те** may be added: *Давайте пойдём в кино! Пойдём в кино! Пойдёмте в кино!* "Actual" verbs of motion such as **идти**, **ехать**, **бежать**, **нести**, although imperfective, have imperatives of this last type: **идёмте**, **едемте**, **бежимте**, **несёмте**.
Infinitive as a command, and the negative imperative

items.text: The infinitive in place of the imperative is used:
points: In case of urgency: *Послать за доктором!*

As a harsh or abrupt form of an order: *Встать!* The negative imperative is, as a rule, in the imperfective aspect: *Берите! Возьмите! — Не берите!* The negative imperative in the perfective aspect has the meaning of a strict warning: *Не забудьте взять ключ! Здесь скользко, не упадите!*
